_quiz_pool.question: What formula calculates speed in motion?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Speed equals distance divided by time.

_quiz_pool.question: What is the unit of speed in SI?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Metres per second (m/s) is the standard SI unit for speed.

_quiz_pool.question: If a river flows 120 m in 20 s, what is its speed?
What does s stand for in v = s ÷ t?
Why do rivers carve deep loops like Goosenecks?
options: Flowing water erodes rock over time
_quiz_pool.explanation: Moving water gradually cuts through rock layers.

_quiz_pool.question: What does t stand for in v = s ÷ t?
Which material is eroded by rivers easily?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Moving water wears away softer rock and soil faster.

_quiz_pool.question: If time increases while distance is constant, speed…
_quiz_pool.explanation: Taking longer to cover the same distance means slower speed.

_quiz_pool.question: What helps monitor water flow in dams?
_quiz_pool.explanation: Sensors and meteorological data help manage water flow safely.

_quiz_pool.question: Water flowing in a river has what main type of energy?

story.title: The winding river of Utah
story.lead: Satellite images highlighted dramatic winding river bends in Utah [1]. Water flowing across the landscape moves rock and soil grain by grain [1].
story.image_caption: Deep river meanders carved into canyon rock
stat.1.label: distance measured along the river channel

stat.3.label: speed of the flowing water stream
story.body_1: Rivers shape Earth over long periods. As water flows down slopes, gravity pulls it forward [1]. Meteorological agencies also track river and dam water levels to keep communities safe from floods [3].
story.body_2: Understanding how fast water moves helps scientists predict erosion and water flow [3]. Fast water carries more sand and gravel, cutting deeper canyons into stone [1].
timeline.1.text: Water gathers in high ground and feeds river channels.
timeline.2.text: Streams rush downhill, gaining speed and carrying sediment.
timeline.3.text: Moving water carves deep loops and canyons into bedrock.
physics.title: Speed, distance and time
physics.body_1: To understand how fast a river flows, we measure two things: how far the water travels and how long it takes. Speed tells us the distance covered in each second.
physics.body_2: If distance increases, speed increases. If time increases for the same distance, speed decreases. We calculate speed by dividing distance by time.
physics.assumptions: We assume water flows at a steady average speed along the straight channel test section.

lab.step_3: Time how many seconds it takes to reach the finish line.
